usage: Used for plant food or garden feed. In everyday Hong Kong Cantonese, 肥料 is a very common countable/uncountable noun depending on context, but learners can treat it as an uncountable mass noun most of the time.
Often appears with gardening verbs like 加, 落, 用, 撒. It refers to something you add to soil or plants to help them grow better.
In casual speech, people may also use it in farming, balcony gardening, or houseplant care. It sounds neutral and practical, not formal.
For beginners, the main tip is to remember it is about nutrients for plants, not animal feed or medicine. The word is widely understood in everyday gardening talk.
